deep.reconstruction:
Setting: a stratified space with two strata. X is a topological surface, the closed stratum Y is a single point a, and the open stratum is X* = X \ {a}. The 'tubular neighbourhood' V_{Y,X} becomes the infinitesimal disc D_a. The deleted neighbourhood V*_{Y,X} becomes the punctured infinitesimal disc D*_a.

Diagram (19) is the span D_a <- D*_a -> X*. The map D*_a -> D_a is annotated as the 'branche-germe dirigé en a', i.e. a germ of the space at a, taken with a direction. Applying the fundamental groupoid functor, the general diagram of groupoids (10) collapses to the span of groups (20):
{1} = pi_1(D_a) <- pi_1(D*_a) -> pi_1(X*).
Here pi_1(D*_a) is written canonically as Z_{a,X}, the 'orientation module of X at a'. It is non-canonically isomorphic to Z, and its two generators correspond to the two local orientations of X at a.

The vertical map Z_{a,X} -> pi_1(X*) sends a generator to the loop around the puncture. It is well defined only up to conjugacy, or as a map of groupoids. Grothendieck says it defines the 'local structure at a' of the fundamental groupoid of X*. In modern terms this is the peripheral (inertia) subgroup: the local monodromy at a.

The previous page gives the data of a sheaf / locally constant system in this situation. In the present case this means a set E_{X*} with a pi_1(X*)-action, a set E_a, and a Z_{a,X}-equivariant map E_a -> E_{X*}, where Z_{a,X} acts trivially on E_a. Equivalently, the map lands in the invariants of the local monodromy. This is the usual description of constructible sheaves on a disc stratified by its centre.

The simplest case (21) is X = C, a = 0, giving the span D_0 <- D*_0 -> C*. Its finite products (C*)^n x C^m-type models (local groups Z^n) are the local 'model types' of stratifications defined by normal crossings divisors in complex analytic geometry.

The next page goes on to identify the category of such systems with presheaves on a small category C. C is built by gluing the three groupoids A = pi_1(V*), B and C = pi_1(X*) with extra arrows from objects of A to objects of B and of C. This is in essence the exit-path category of the stratified space, and the stratified homotopy type is encoded as a presheaf topos.
errors: No mathematical error. Minor imprecision: Z_{a,X} -> pi_1(X*) needs a base point, so it is defined only up to conjugation; Grothendieck sidesteps this by working with groupoids. The reference '(2)' for the vertical homomorphism should be (20).

D_a is called a 'disque (infinitésimal)'. In pure topology its fundamental group is trivial and the construction is homotopy-invariant, so this is fine as a germ notion. No rigorous definition is given here.

ideas.what: Stratified space with point stratum encoded by the span of fundamental groupoids pi_1(D_a) <- pi_1(D*_a) -> pi_1(X*) (diagram (10) specialized to (20))
ideas.modern_name: Exit-path category / stratified fundamental category; gluing data (link groupoid mapping to the stratum groupoids)
ideas.usually_credited_to: MacPherson (exit paths, 1990s, unpublished); Treumann (2009); Lurie (Higher Algebra, appendix A); Woolf (2009)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5-6, discusses dévissage of stratified structures and tubular neighbourhoods qualitatively, but not this explicit groupoid-span description

ideas.what: Canonical 'orientation module' Z_{a,X} ≅ Z, whose generators are the local orientations at a, used in place of Z
ideas.modern_name: Local fundamental group of the punctured neighbourhood / inertia; topological analogue of Z(1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; Z(1) notation from Grothendieck school / SGA
ideas.where_published: SGA 1 / SGA 4-5 (Z(1), tame inertia); Esquisse (Ẑ(1) in the anabelian context)

ideas.what: Local monodromy homomorphism Z_{a,X} -> pi_1(X*) as the 'local structure at a' of the fundamental groupoid of X*
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Riemann, Picard-Lefschetz); for curves, Grothendieck's SGA1 description of tame fundamental groups

ideas.what: Products of the model C ⊃ C* give the local model types of normal crossings stratifications
ideas.modern_name: Local model of an NCD complement, pi_1 = Z^n locally
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck-Murre, LNM 208 (tame fundamental group of NCD complements); SGA 7

missed.claim: This page and its neighbours describe the stratified homotopy type of a two-stratum space as a gluing of groupoids along the link groupoid, with locally constant / constructible systems being presheaves on the resulting category (F ≃ Ĉ on the next page). This is an early explicit form of the exit-path category picture of constructible sheaves, usually credited to MacPherson / Treumann / Lurie.
missed.quote: L'homomorphisme vertical de (20) est l'homomorphisme qui définit la structure "locale en a" du groupoïde fondamental X*
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck's independent formulation of the exit-path / stratified homotopy hypothesis, which bears on historical credit. The span-of-groupoids formulation with a canonical orientation module is close to later 'decorated' stratified homotopy theory, but adds nothing technically new.

deep.surprise_reason: The content of this page itself (punctured disc, local monodromy, NCD models) is classical. Its interest lies in context: it is part of an unpublished development of a stratified topos / exit-path-category description that predates or parallels the later literature. That is a modest historical point, not a new result.
transcription_corrections: The '6' / 'δ[?]' at the top right is the manuscript's own page number (6), not part of diagram (19).
The annotation on the arrow in (19) reads approximately '"branche-germe dirigé en a"' (a directed germ at a); the reading is uncertain.
'Le cas le plus simple est celui où' is followed by (21) 'X = C plan complexe, a = {0}', then 'd'où D*_0 -> D_0, ↓ C*' (rendered with ℂ*).
